lines.L01: Sample A crosses the line at cycle {cqA0}, sample B at {cqB0}.
lines.L02: Which one had more target to begin with?
lines.L03: Each cycle, heat separates the strands; on cooling, primers bind and a polymerase builds new strands.
lines.L04: So the target roughly doubles every cycle.
lines.L05: The thermal cycler: tube strip, heated lid, and a Peltier block that switches temperatures.
lines.L06: Every cycle, the excitation source shines through the excitation filter into the tube.
lines.L07: The dye’s fluorescence passes the emission filter to the detector.
lines.L08: Fluorescence grows with the product: the amplification curve.
lines.L09: Cq is the cycle where it crosses the threshold — the lower the Cq, the more starting target.
lines.L10: Trace contamination can give false results, and no amplification does not prove a negative.
lines.L11: In LabGuide: Lab → Instruments and methods → Molecular diagnostics → Real-time PCR.
lines.L12: This schematic, its numbered parts, and the principle — with sources.
lines.L13: Limitations and contamination control are on the card too.
lines.L14: Read the curve, not just the Cq.
lines.L15: LabGuide — Lab → Instruments and methods → Real-time PCR.
